[b][size=xx-large][color=#ffffff][u]Hack Forum News - Edition 70[/u][/color][/size][/b]

[b]Welcome back to another Hack Forum News edition. Where we keep you up to date on the weekly events and news happening on site and around the world. If you have never heard of the Hack Forum News, don't worry, we have you covered. We are a team of members from the Hack Forums community who are journalists and writers, and we are here to keep you in the loop of the changes around the site and the events happening around the world.[/b]

[hr]

[img]https://hackforums.net/images/hfnews/headlines-red.png[/img]
[size=medium][b]Writer -[/b][/size] [mention=2745296]

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6333781][color=#ffffff]Convo Returns[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

After being taken down for development [mention=1] has brought back the Convo feature. While everything is running and functional members should expect some minor bugs over the first couple of days as development continues and remaining bugs are ironed out. Have you jumped into convo and tested the update yet?

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6334034][color=#ffffff]Tether Payment Support[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

Following frequent member requests to pay invoices with Tether [mention=1] has integrated Plisio to the forum. The new payment option is currently live for Features with full support rolling out to all remaining invoice purchases over the next 24 hours. Through Plisio members can now check out using Tron, BSC, ETH, and SOL, along side Tether support across the TRON, BSC, ETH, and SOL networks. Which network will you be using for your future upgrades? Share your thoughts and feedback in the original thread.

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6334081][color=#ffffff]/Dev/Null:Ports Game[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

After previously pulling the plug on the game due to an overwhelming number of bugs, [mention=1] is considering bringing the project back from the dead. With modern AI coding tools capable of tackling the issues and getting the system fully operational in an estimated 1 to 2 days, the question comes down to if community interest justifies the effort. Is a revival worth the dev time or should it remain retired? Share your thoughts and feedback in the original thread.

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6333691][color=#ffffff]Rack Attack[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

Taking site gamification to a whole new level [mention=1] has just launched Rack Attack across the forum. Featuring 10 escalating stages designed to test your skills members are encouraged to jump in early and start practicing before things get truly competitive. Have you put your skills to the test yet, and what level have you managed to reach?

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]Tesla unveiled its next-generation Roadster[/color][/size][/b][/u]

Tesla unveiled its next generation roadster this week with rocket style thrusters similar to ones used by spaceX. The demonstration showed the Roadster using high pressure gas thrusters to launch, flip in mid-air and land. This is a real engineering demonstration, but it doesn't establish that the vehicle is ready for ordinary flying-car use.

[b][url=https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-set-unveil-next-generation-roadster-sports-ev-after-years-delay-2026-10-15]Source[/url][/b]

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]RAM and SSD prices are still under pressure[/color][/size][/b][/u]

The latest market forecasts point to conventional DRAM contract prices rising 10–15% and NAND flash prices 15–20% in Q4 2026. AI data centres are competing for memory and storage capacity, leaving less room for cheaper consumer components.

[b][url=https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260930-13258.html?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block]Source[/url][/b]

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]RAM and SSD prices are still under pressure[/color][/size][/b][/u]

Chips and AI related stocks bounced on 19 October after a difficult week. Investors are increasingly concerned about whether enormous AI infrastructure investments will generate enough profit to justify their costs.

[b][url=https://www.reuters.com/business/wall-st-futures-climb-ai-stocks-rebound-oil-yields-fall-2026-10-19]Source[/url][/b]

[hr]

[img]https://hackforums.net/images/hfnews/w-movies.png[/img]
[size=medium][b]Writer -[/b][/size] [mention=2331053]

[b]This weeks Movie Of The Week:[/b]
[i]Buddy 2026[/i]

[b]Trailer:[/b]
[video=youtube]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eGe4BEnsjco[/video]

This movie was submitted on our Submision thread [b][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6318534][color=#ffffff][HF News] Movie Of The Week Submissions[/color][/url][/b]

This week's submission is thanks to [mention=123]

This week's movie of the week of the week might not be for everyone as it has a trait to be a little scary, but as it's the spooky time of year, we saw this being posted and knew we had to share it this week.

The movie is based on a little girl who is with her friends, but they are trapped inside a kids TV show and must find a way to escape. It itself was rated a strong seven out of ten by Charlie for it being an original concept compared to some of the newer releases we have seen this year. You can also check out what others think about it in Charlie's thread. [url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6333801]Buddy 2026[/url] Let us know if you are thinking of checking this one out or if you think it might be a little bit to scary for you in the replies below.
